edited_rows.rationale: V. 4 turns from personal testimony to a congregational summons, “Sing praise to Yahweh, you saints of his. Give thanks to his holy name.” (web:Ps.30.4), grounded in the maxim that follows, “For his anger is but for a moment. His favor is for a lifetime. Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.” (web:Ps.30.5). V. 6 returns to the psalmist's own voice with a new temporal marker, “As for me, I said in my prosperity, "I shall never be moved."” (web:Ps.30.6).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Keeping vv. 4-5 with the testimony that precedes them is also defensible, since the summons still addresses the congregation about Yahweh's saving acts already narrated; this candidate isolates the maxim on its own imperative-plus-vocative opening.
observed_substrate_signals: imperative זַמְּר֣וּ ("sing praise") plus vocative addressee "you saints of his" opens v. 4, shifting from Yahweh-directed address to a congregational summons (web:Ps.30.4 = oshb:Ps.30.5)
the moment/lifetime, night/morning antitheses of v. 5 state the maxim grounding the summons before the narrative resumes at v. 6
edited_rows.device_notes: The night-to-morning maxim of v. 5 anticipates the psalm's own mourning-to-dancing resolution at its close. A zamar-root inclusio also brackets the two strophes: the summons's opening imperative, זַמְּר֣וּ ("sing praise", web:Ps.30.4 = oshb:Ps.30.5), recurs in the psalm's closing verse, יְזַמֶּרְךָ֣ ("may sing praise to you", web:Ps.30.12 = oshb:Ps.30.13).

edited_rows.rationale: V. 6 returns to the psalmist's own voice with a temporal marker, “As for me, I said in my prosperity, "I shall never be moved."” (web:Ps.30.6), narrating the reversal that follows — Yahweh hiding his face (web:Ps.30.7) and the embedded cry quoted directly through v. 10, “Hear, Yahweh, and have mercy on me. Yahweh, be my helper."” (web:Ps.30.10) — before the psalm resolves in present-tense testimony, “You have turned my mourning into dancing for me. You have removed my sackcloth, and clothed me with gladness,” (web:Ps.30.11), closing with thanksgiving forever (web:Ps.30.12).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Splitting vv. 6-7 (narrative setup), vv. 8-10 (the quoted cry), and vv. 11-12 (resolution) into three rows is also defensible on the same narrative movement; this candidate keeps the reversal-and-resolution arc as one row bounded by the congregational summons before it.
observed_substrate_signals: the psalmist's own voice (וַ֭אֲנִי אָמַ֣רְתִּי, "and I, I said") opens v. 6, marking the narrative's start (web:Ps.30.6 = oshb:Ps.30.7)
a direct quotation runs vv. 9-10 in the WEB's own punctuation, embedded inside the narrated cry of v. 8
the resolution verb הָפַ֣כְתָּ ("you have turned") opens v. 11, answering the reversal narrated from v. 6 (web:Ps.30.11 = oshb:Ps.30.12)
edited_rows.device_notes: A zamar-root inclusio brackets this strophe with the summons that precedes it: this closing verse's יְזַמֶּרְךָ֣ ("may sing praise to you", web:Ps.30.12 = oshb:Ps.30.13) answers the opening imperative זַמְּר֣וּ ("sing praise", web:Ps.30.4 = oshb:Ps.30.5); no shared root links this closing verse to the psalm's own opening verse (web:Ps.30.1), which instead uses the extolling verb rum.

edited_rows.rationale: The superscription “For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David.” opens the psalm at web:Ps.31.0 (oshb:Ps.31.1). The strophe itself opens the refuge plea with בְּךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה חָ֭סִיתִי (oshb:Ps.31.2) “In you, Yahweh, I take refuge” at web:Ps.31.1, vocative fused directly to the verb, then runs a cluster of second-person imperatives, הַטֵּ֤ה אֵלַ֨י אָזְנְךָ֮ מְהֵרָ֪ה הַצִּ֫ילֵ֥נִי הֱיֵ֤ה לִ֨י לְֽצוּר מָ֭עוֹז לְבֵ֥ית מְצוּד֗וֹת לְהוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי (oshb:Ps.31.3) “Bow down your ear to me. Deliver me speedily. Be to me a strong rock, a house of defense to save me” (web:Ps.31.2). The mood pivots at web:Ps.31.5 with בְּיָדְךָ֮ אַפְקִ֪יד ר֫וּחִ֥י (oshb:Ps.31.6) “Into your hand I commend my spirit.” This self-consecration clause is followed by testimony that closes the strophe — “You have known my soul in adversities” (web:Ps.31.7) and “You have set my feet in a large place” (web:Ps.31.8) — reporting deliverance already granted rather than still being requested.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: A break after web:Ps.31.4 was weighed and set aside: the imperative petitions run unbroken in verb mood and addressee from web:Ps.31.1 through the self-consecration clause at web:Ps.31.5, which itself renews the vocative address, פָּדִ֖יתָה אוֹתִ֥י יְהוָ֗ה אֵ֣ל אֱמֶֽת (oshb:Ps.31.6) “You redeem me, Yahweh, God of truth” (web:Ps.31.5); the strophe's next vocative renewal after that falls at web:Ps.31.9, already inside the imperative petition that opens the next strophe.
observed_substrate_signals: בְּךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה חָ֭סִיתִי (oshb:Ps.31.2) fuses the vocative to the opening verb, matching the strophe's position immediately after the title

הַטֵּ֤ה אֵלַ֨י אָזְנְךָ֮ מְהֵרָ֪ה הַצִּ֫ילֵ֥נִי הֱיֵ֤ה לִ֨י לְֽצוּר מָ֭עוֹז לְבֵ֥ית מְצוּד֗וֹת לְהוֹשִׁיעֵֽנִי (oshb:Ps.31.3) runs consecutive second-person imperatives through the strophe's opening half
בְּיָדְךָ֮ אַפְקִ֪יד ר֫וּחִ֥י (oshb:Ps.31.6) shifts the verb mood from imperative petition to singular self-consecration, the strophe's hinge
edited_rows.device_notes: These rows resolve upward to Psalm 31 as parent. The title carries the mizmor, lamnatseach, and le-David genre labels (psalm_device_inventory.json), tier-1 opener evidence dual-cited at web:Ps.31.0 = oshb:Ps.31.1.

edited_rows.rationale: A fresh petition opens at web:Ps.31.9 with חָנֵּ֥נִי יְהוָה֮ (oshb:Ps.31.10) “Have mercy on me, Yahweh,” an imperative-plus-vocative pairing that reopens the address to God after the testimony register of web:Ps.31.7-Ps.31.8. The strophe stays in singular distress description — bones wasting, life spent with sorrow (web:Ps.31.10), contempt among neighbors (web:Ps.31.11) — and closes with נִ֭שְׁכַּחְתִּי כְּמֵ֣ת מִלֵּ֑ב (oshb:Ps.31.13) “I am forgotten from their hearts like a dead man” (web:Ps.31.12), completing the isolation image before the adversative pivot at web:Ps.31.14.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Folding web:Ps.31.9-13 into the preceding strophe was rejected because חָנֵּ֥נִי יְהוָה֮ (oshb:Ps.31.10) restarts the imperative-plus-vocative petition form after the declarative testimony of web:Ps.31.7-8, marking a return to distress rather than a continuation of it.
observed_substrate_signals: חָנֵּ֥נִי יְהוָה֮ (oshb:Ps.31.10) repeats the imperative-plus-vocative petition form of the psalm's own opener
נִ֭שְׁכַּחְתִּי כְּמֵ֣ת מִלֵּ֑ב (oshb:Ps.31.13) closes the strophe on an isolation image before the adversative pivot that opens web:Ps.31.14
edited_rows.device_notes: The strophe's distress vocabulary (bones, contempt, oblivion) belongs to the same Davidic lament register named at the title; no further psalm-level device touches this span.

edited_rows.rationale: The pronoun-fronted וַאֲנִ֤י עָלֶ֣יךָ בָטַ֣חְתִּי יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.31.15) “But I trust in you, Yahweh” opens web:Ps.31.14 with the adversative pronoun fronting the clause, a contrastive pivot after the isolation close of web:Ps.31.13. Trust language carries through “My times are in your hand” (web:Ps.31.15) into a renewed petition for deliverance from enemies (web:Ps.31.15-16), then closes with an imprecation against שִׂפְתֵ֫י שָׁ֥קֶר (oshb:Ps.31.19) “the lying lips” that speak “against the righteous insolently” (web:Ps.31.18).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Extending the prior strophe through web:Ps.31.14 was rejected: וַאֲנִ֤י (oshb:Ps.31.15) fronts the clause precisely where the isolation testimony of web:Ps.31.13 ends, and the trust declaration it introduces governs the petitions that follow rather than extending the lament catalogue.
observed_substrate_signals: וַאֲנִ֤י (oshb:Ps.31.15) fronts the independent pronoun against the preceding third-person image, marking the adversative turn; the same pronoun (וַאֲנִ֤י, oshb:Ps.31.23) recurs mid-strophe at web:Ps.31.22, inside the strophe that follows this one, without marking a seam there
שִׂפְתֵ֫י שָׁ֥קֶר (oshb:Ps.31.19) closes the strophe on an imprecation against slanderous speech, distinct from the petition-for-self register that opens it
edited_rows.device_notes: No selah, acrostic, or doxology device touches this strophe; the adversative-pronoun pivot is a syntactic, not a marks-layer, signal.

edited_rows.rationale: The closing couplet turns from addressing Yahweh to addressing the congregation: אֶֽהֱב֥וּ אֶת יְהוָ֗ה כָּֽל חֲסִ֫ידָ֥יו (oshb:Ps.31.24) “Oh love Yahweh, all you his saints!” opens web:Ps.31.23 with a plural imperative and a third-person referent for God (“his saints”, not “you”), and חִ֭זְקוּ וְיַאֲמֵ֣ץ (oshb:Ps.31.25) “Be strong, and let your heart take courage” continues the same congregational address through the psalm's close at web:Ps.31.24.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Reading web:Ps.31.23-24 as a continuation of the praise strophe was rejected because the addressee changes from Yahweh — second person through most of web:Ps.31.19-22, but third person at the berakhah formula itself, בָּר֥וּךְ (oshb:Ps.31.22) “Praise be to Yahweh, for he has shown me his marvelous loving kindness” (web:Ps.31.21) — to “his saints” (web:Ps.31.23) and “you who hope in Yahweh” (web:Ps.31.24), a shift in who is spoken to rather than what is said about God.
observed_substrate_signals: אֶֽהֱב֥וּ אֶת יְהוָ֗ה כָּֽל חֲסִ֫ידָ֥יו (oshb:Ps.31.24) is a plural imperative addressed to “all you his saints” (web:Ps.31.23), not to Yahweh directly — the divine referent is embedded via the third-person possessive suffix (“his”) rather than a direct second-person address to God
חִ֭זְקוּ (oshb:Ps.31.25) sustains the plural-imperative congregational address through the psalm's final verse
edited_rows.device_notes: The psalm closes without a book-boundary doxology; the exhortation functions as this composition's own coda-like exit, kept here as strophe rather than coda since that unit_type is reserved for the four book-seam doxology closes.

edited_rows.rationale: The title “By David. A contemplative psalm.” sits inside MT v1 for this identity psalm, dual-cited web:Ps.32.0 = oshb:Ps.32.1 (maskil, le-David labels; psalm_device_inventory.json). The strophe opens with the paired beatitude אַשְׁרֵ֥י (oshb:Ps.32.1) “Blessed is he” and אַ֥שְֽׁרֵי אָדָ֗ם (oshb:Ps.32.2) “Blessed is the man” (web:Ps.32.1-2), pivots to singular confession at web:Ps.32.3 — כִּֽי הֶ֭חֱרַשְׁתִּי (oshb:Ps.32.3) “When I kept silence” — and moves through disclosure of sin (web:Ps.32.5) into instruction for “everyone who is godly” (web:Ps.32.6). Selah marks web:Ps.32.4, web:Ps.32.5, and closes the strophe at web:Ps.32.7, corroborating the pause before the divine speech that opens web:Ps.32.8.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Splitting the beatitude (web:Ps.32.1-2) from the confession (web:Ps.32.3-7) into separate rows was rejected: the beatitude states the blessing the confession then narrates receiving, and no addressee or speaker shift separates them — no speaker change occurs before web:Ps.32.8.
observed_substrate_signals: אַשְׁרֵ֥י (oshb:Ps.32.1) opens the psalm's ashrei beatitude particle
אַ֥שְֽׁרֵי אָדָ֗ם (oshb:Ps.32.2) repeats the same ashrei beatitude particle one verse later
כִּֽי הֶ֭חֱרַשְׁתִּי (oshb:Ps.32.3) shifts from third-person maxim to singular confession without changing addressee
selah closes three verses of this seven-verse strophe (Ps.32.4, Ps.32.5, Ps.32.7 in pmarks_Ps.json), the three placed within this span
edited_rows.device_notes: The parent unit here is the full Psalm 32. Its eleven verses carry three of the book's 71 selah instances, together placed inside this psalm's span. Ps 32 also carries 5 paseq segs (a seg-layer, single-witness mark: MT 32:4, 32:6, 32:7, 32:8, and 32:9); the first three of these (MT 32:4, 32:6, 32:7) fall inside this row's own span.

edited_rows.rationale: Psalm 33 carries no WEB title and opens directly with an imperative cluster: רַנְּנ֣וּ צַ֭דִּיקִים בַּֽיהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.33.1) “Rejoice in Yahweh, you righteous!” (web:Ps.33.1), הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.33.2) “Give thanks to Yahweh” (web:Ps.33.2), and שִֽׁירוּ ל֭וֹ (oshb:Ps.33.3) “Sing to him” (web:Ps.33.3), three consecutive plural imperatives addressed to the congregation. This is the psalm's opener evidence, functionally parallel to the superscriptions that open titled psalms even though Psalm 33 carries no title.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Extending the imperative strophe through web:Ps.33.9 was rejected: the call-to-worship imperatives addressed to the congregation end at web:Ps.33.3, and web:Ps.33.4 opens a motive clause moving to third-person declaration about Yahweh. The nearest comparable volitive form after that is the jussive יִֽירְא֣וּ (web:Ps.33.8 = oshb:Ps.33.8) “Let all the earth fear Yahweh”, addressed to the whole earth rather than the congregation of “you righteous” (web:Ps.33.1); no further plural imperative addressed to a congregation recurs anywhere later in the psalm, including at its close (web:Ps.33.20-22, which is declarative throughout except for the 3ms jussive יְהִֽי (oshb:Ps.33.22, ‘let it be’), at web:Ps.33.22).
observed_substrate_signals: three verse-initial plural imperatives — רַנְּנ֣וּ (web:Ps.33.1 = oshb:Ps.33.1), הוֹד֣וּ (web:Ps.33.2 = oshb:Ps.33.2), שִֽׁירוּ (web:Ps.33.3 = oshb:Ps.33.3) — open the psalm, with two further plural imperatives closing v.2 (זַמְּרוּ) and inside v.3 (הֵיטִ֥יבוּ), five in all across the span; the addressee named is צַ֭דִּיקִים (web:Ps.33.1 = oshb:Ps.33.1) “you righteous”, not a divine vocative
web:Ps.33.4 opens with כִּֽי (oshb:Ps.33.4), a motive-clause particle shifting from imperative address to declarative predication
edited_rows.device_notes: Under Psalm 33 the rows form one family. The psalm's 22 verses match the Hebrew alphabet's count, but the acrostics table in psalm_device_inventory.json carries no entry for Psalm 33 (its keyed psalms are 9, 10, 25, 34, 37, 111, 112, 119, 145) — no acrostic scheme is claimed for this psalm; the imperative cluster of web:Ps.33.1-3 is the opener evidence instead.

edited_rows.rationale: A beatitude formula reopens the psalm's third movement: אַשְׁרֵ֣י הַ֭גּוֹי (oshb:Ps.33.12) “Blessed is the nation” at web:Ps.33.12, the same ashrei particle that opens Psalm 32 (web:Ps.32.1-2). From the elect nation the unit widens to Yahweh's oversight of humankind (web:Ps.33.13-15), the futility of military strength (web:Ps.33.16-17), and closes on הִנֵּ֤ה עֵ֣ין יְ֭הוָה (oshb:Ps.33.18) “Behold, Yahweh's eye is on those who fear him” (web:Ps.33.18), extending through deliverance “from death” and “famine” at web:Ps.33.19.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Merging this span with the preceding word/creation unit was rejected: אַשְׁרֵ֣י (oshb:Ps.33.12) reopens the beatitude form used once already in this psalm's companion at web:Ps.32.1-2, a formulaic opener the intervening counsel-versus-counsel antithesis of web:Ps.33.10-11 does not carry.
observed_substrate_signals: אַשְׁרֵ֣י (oshb:Ps.33.12) reopens the beatitude particle after the resolved antithesis of web:Ps.33.11
הִנֵּ֤ה עֵ֣ין יְ֭הוָה (oshb:Ps.33.18) opens the strophe's closing unit with a presentative particle shifting the focus to those who fear Yahweh, closing on deliverance from death and famine
edited_rows.device_notes: The ashrei opener at web:Ps.33.12 reuses, in its own wording, the same beatitude particle already seen at web:Ps.32.1-2 in the preceding psalm of this part; the two uses are treated as texture, not as a cross-psalm boundary relation.

edited_rows.rationale: A person shift closes the psalm: נַ֭פְשֵׁנוּ חִכְּתָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.33.20) “Our soul has waited for Yahweh” opens web:Ps.33.20 with נַ֭פְשֵׁנוּ, a noun (“soul”) bearing the first-person-plural possessive suffix (“our”), governing the third-person-feminine-singular verb חִכְּתָ֣ה (“has waited”, agreeing with the feminine noun nefesh); this plural self-reference is not used earlier in the psalm, replacing the third-person “he/his” language of web:Ps.33.13-19 with a congregational “we/our” voice that continues through the closing petition יְהִֽי חַסְדְּךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה עָלֵ֑ינוּ (oshb:Ps.33.22) “Let your loving kindness be on us, Yahweh” (web:Ps.33.22).
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Treating web:Ps.33.20-22 as a continuation of the providence unit was rejected: the pronoun shifts from third-person “him/his” description of Yahweh's oversight to a plural “our/we” congregational address, a change in speaker voice the preceding eight verses do not share.
observed_substrate_signals: נַ֭פְשֵׁנוּ (oshb:Ps.33.20) is a noun (‘soul’) with a first-person-plural possessive suffix (‘our’), taking the third-person-feminine-singular finite verb חִכְּתָ֣ה (‘has waited’, web:Ps.33.20); this plural self-reference is not used earlier in the psalm, against “he/his” forms in the immediately preceding span
יְהִֽי חַסְדְּךָ֣ (oshb:Ps.33.22) closes the psalm on a jussive petition in the same congregational voice
edited_rows.device_notes: This closing strophe carries no selah, doxology, or acrostic marker; Psalm 33's parent grouping (stated at web:Ps.33.1-3) covers this row as it does the rest of the psalm's rows.

edited_rows.rationale: The title “By David; when he pretended to be insane before Abimelech, who drove him away, and he departed” opens the psalm at web:Ps.34.0 (oshb:Ps.34.1) — title material naming the Abimelech episode, not a narrative row. Psalm 34 is acrostic (psalm_device_inventory.json: waw absent from the letter sequence) beginning אֲבָרֲכָ֣ה אֶת יְהוָ֣ה בְּכָל עֵ֑ת (oshb:Ps.34.2) “I will bless Yahweh at all times” (web:Ps.34.1), alef; בַּ֭יהוָה תִּתְהַלֵּ֣ל נַפְשִׁ֑י (oshb:Ps.34.3) “My soul shall boast in Yahweh” (web:Ps.34.2), bet; גַּדְּל֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה אִתִּ֑י (oshb:Ps.34.4) “Oh magnify Yahweh with me” (web:Ps.34.3), gimel — a communal invitation opening the strophe.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Merging web:Ps.34.1-3 with web:Ps.34.4-7 was rejected: the communal invitation register (‘with me’, ‘let's exalt’ together) closes at web:Ps.34.3 — the psalm's one cohortative verb, וּנְרוֹמְמָ֖ה (oshb:Ps.34.4), occurs inside this row's own span (it occurs exactly once in the psalm) and does not recur later — and web:Ps.34.4 turns instead to individual singular testimony, “I sought Yahweh, and he answered me”
observed_substrate_signals: the strophe's three verses open the acrostic's first three letters alef, bet, gimel (byte-checked against web:Ps.34.1-3; sweep: 22 verses, waw the acrostic's only gap per psalm_device_inventory.json)

וּנְרוֹמְמָ֖ה שְׁמ֣וֹ יַחְדָּֽו (oshb:Ps.34.4) closes the strophe on the cohortative “Let's exalt his name together” (web:Ps.34.3), the final plural-cohortative verb before individual testimony resumes
edited_rows.device_notes: Psalm 34's rows answer to one shared parent grouping across this part. The historical title names Abimelech (1 Sam 21 material, kept as title text and not quoted as narrative); the acrostic surface is byte-confirmed alef through gimel here and continues waw-less through this psalm's remaining rows.

edited_rows.rationale: An imperative pair addressed to Yahweh's own worshippers reopens web:Ps.34.8, tet: טַעֲמ֣וּ וּ֭רְאוּ כִּי ט֣וֹב יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ps.34.9) “Oh taste and see that Yahweh is good”. This is followed by יְר֣אוּ אֶת יְהוָ֣ה קְדֹשָׁ֑יו (oshb:Ps.34.10) “Oh fear Yahweh, you his saints” (web:Ps.34.9), yod. The strophe closes on the young-lions wisdom contrast at web:Ps.34.10, kaf: כְּ֭פִירִים רָשׁ֣וּ (oshb:Ps.34.11) “The young lions do lack, and suffer hunger”.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: Folding web:Ps.34.8-10 into the following “children” address (web:Ps.34.11-14) was rejected: the taste-and-see and fear-Yahweh imperatives here address Yahweh's own worshippers, embedded as קְדֹשָׁ֑יו “his saints” (oshb:Ps.34.10, web:Ps.34.9), while web:Ps.34.11 opens with a different named vocative, “children” — a change in addressed party, not a shift from unaddressed to addressed, a distinction the wisdom-lion contrast at web:Ps.34.10 does not share with either.
observed_substrate_signals: טַעֲמ֣וּ וּ֭רְאוּ (oshb:Ps.34.9) and יְר֣אוּ אֶת יְהוָ֣ה קְדֹשָׁ֑יו (oshb:Ps.34.10) form a two-verse imperative cluster addressed to Yahweh's worshippers, קְדֹשָׁ֑יו “his saints” (web:Ps.34.9), an addressee embedded via a third-person possessive suffix rather than a separately named vocative
כְּ֭פִירִים רָשׁ֣וּ (oshb:Ps.34.11) closes the strophe on a wisdom antithesis (lions lack, seekers of Yahweh do not) preceding the vocative shift at web:Ps.34.11
edited_rows.device_notes: These letters (tet, yod, kaf) continue the byte-confirmed acrostic sequence past the waw gap disclosed in the preceding strophe; no further irregularity falls in this span.

edited_rows.rationale: The unit opens with a transgression oracle that the psalmist locates in his own heart, נְאֻֽם פֶּ֣שַׁע לָ֭רָשָׁע בְּקֶ֣רֶב (web:Ps.36.1 = oshb:Ps.36.2) “A revelation is within my heart about the disobedience of the wicked” — בְּקֶ֣רֶב (“within my heart”) carries a first-person-singular suffix, the psalmist's own heart, not the wicked man's; the verse's own second half turns to the wicked man's eyes in the third person, “There is no fear of God before his eyes.” (web:Ps.36.1). Third-person “he”/“his” description of the wicked continues through web:Ps.36.4 = oshb:Ps.36.5, closing on דִּבְרֵי (oshb:Ps.36.4) “The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit. He has ceased to be wise and to do good.” (web:Ps.36.3) and אָ֤וֶן יַחְשֹׁ֗ב עַֽל (oshb:Ps.36.5) “He plots iniquity on his bed” (web:Ps.36.4); the address then turns to second-person praise of Yahweh at web:Ps.36.5 = oshb:Ps.36.6 — a discourse-frame change from oracle-about-the-wicked to hymn.
edited_rows.rejected_alternative: web:Ps.36.4 = oshb:Ps.36.5 could be read as transitional rather than part of the oracle unit, but it keeps the same third-person subject as web:Ps.36.1-Ps.36.3 = oshb:Ps.36.2-Ps.36.4, with no addressee change.
observed_substrate_signals: נְאֻֽם (web:Ps.36.1 = oshb:Ps.36.2) opens the unit on a term elsewhere marking formal oracular speech, located in the psalmist's own heart (בְּקֶ֣רֶב, first-person-singular suffix) and directed at the wicked man's conduct, not lodged in the wicked man's own heart

edited_rows.rationale: Second-person address to Yahweh opens the unit, “Your loving kindness, Yahweh, is in the heavens.” (web:Ps.36.5 = oshb:Ps.36.6), replacing the third-person “he” of the oracle unit; loving-kindness (חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ, oshb:Ps.36.6) and righteousness (צִדְקָֽתְךָ֨, oshb:Ps.36.7) recur toward web:Ps.36.10 = oshb:Ps.36.11, while faithfulness (אֱ֝מֽוּנָתְךָ֗, oshb:Ps.36.6, ‘your faithfulness’) occurs in exactly 1 verse of the span, web:Ps.36.5 = oshb:Ps.36.6, and does not recur; the closing petition, “Don't let the foot of pride come against me.” (web:Ps.36.11 = oshb:Ps.36.12), and the psalm's final report, “There the workers of iniquity are fallen… and shall not be able to rise” (web:Ps.36.12 = oshb:Ps.36.13), drop the second-person suffix altogether but remain this same unit, since nothing in the psalm reopens a fresh discourse frame after web:Ps.36.5 = oshb:Ps.36.6 before its close.

observed_substrate_signals: second-person “Your”/“you” address to Yahweh, marked by second-person-masculine-singular suffixed forms (חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ “your loving kindness”), opens web:Ps.36.5 = oshb:Ps.36.6 and runs through web:Ps.36.10 = oshb:Ps.36.11; the closing two verses, web:Ps.36.11-Ps.36.12 = oshb:Ps.36.12-Ps.36.13, carry no “you”/“your” form in either witness — the first a jussive petition with third-person subjects (“the foot of pride”, “the hand of the wicked”) and first-person-singular object suffixes, the second a fully third-person report, “the workers of iniquity… fallen… shall not be able to rise”

edited_rows.rationale: נ opens web:Ps.37.25, נַ֤עַר (oshb:Ps.37.25) “I have been young, and now am old, yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken”; ס opens web:Ps.37.27, ס֣וּר (oshb:Ps.37.27) “Depart from evil, and do good.” The acrostic's structural sequence then continues regularly through this span's close: פ opens web:Ps.37.30, פִּֽי צַ֭דִּיק (oshb:Ps.37.30) “The mouth of the righteous talks of wisdom”, with ayin absent between the samekh and pe positions (matching the acrostic's own missing-letter table), and צ opens web:Ps.37.32, צוֹפֶ֣ה רָ֭שָׁע לַצַּדִּ֑יק (oshb:Ps.37.32) “The wicked watch the righteous” — pe before tsade, the regular alphabetic order. edited_rows.rationale: This row opens mid-way through the acrostic's tsade span: tsade's full structural span runs two verses, MT 37:32-33, straddling the seam with the row before it, and this row's own opening pronouns, “him” / “he” (oshb:Ps.37.33), grammatically depend on ‘the righteous’ (tsaddiq) named at MT 37:32, one verse outside this row's own span. ק opens web:Ps.37.34, “Wait for Yahweh, and keep his way”; ר opens web:Ps.37.35, “I have seen the wicked in great power”; ש opens web:Ps.37.37, “Mark the perfect man, and see the upright”; tav never occupies a structural position in this acrostic — consistent with 5 of the book's 9 acrostic psalms, where tav likewise never reaches a structural position — though tav does occur once as a surface (non-structural) letter, at MT 37:31. The content closes the psalm on one continuous movement — Yahweh will not abandon the righteous (web:Ps.37.33), the call to wait and watch the wicked's end (web:Ps.37.34-Ps.37.36), and the righteous's future against the wicked's cutting-off (web:Ps.37.37-Ps.37.40) — giving the psalm's closing row one continuous content arc.
